conventions.convention: The ordered factorization is H1 = H2 ⊗ HE; partial trace removes HE, yielding both rho2 and sigma2. Both reference states are positive definite; the rho states may be singular.
Natural logarithms give dimensionless entropy in nats, with 0 log 0 = 0. Ki = −log sigmai and Deltai = tr((rhoi − sigmai)Ki). The adopted balance has sign a2 − a1 = Delta1 − Delta2.
Sgen,i = kB[ai + s(rhoi) − s(sigmai)], with kB > 0 in J/K. The ai are supplied geometric entropy data, without an asserted area identification.
The limit conclusion requires finite convergence of both endpoint entropy sequences in one fixed scheme. Neither convergence nor regulator independence is established.

The geometry is a supplied smooth null hypersurface with future affine generator and compact transverse spacelike cuts; cut labels order the model data without asserting a global event-horizon property.

load_bearing.statement: Adopt finite nested state data with rho2 = TrE rho1, sigma2 = TrE sigma1, faithful reference states, a2 − a1 = Delta1 − Delta2, and Sgen,i = kB[ai + s(rhoi) − s(sigmai)]. These are model premises, without a continuum or area-calibration claim.

For every finite-regulator data set satisfying the nested balance postulate, Sgen,2 − Sgen,1 = kB[D(rho1 || sigma1) − D(rho2 || sigma2)] ≥ 0. If such data sets satisfy the postulate term by term in one fixed scheme and both endpoint sequences converge finitely to Li, then L2 ≥ L1.
